title: Press Kit Upload
description: A batch uploader where each file's preview develops out of blur as its ring fills, so progress is something you see rather than only read. It opens mid-flight — one file landed, two climbing — then the video drops its connection at 61%, freezes its ring red, and waits for a retry that rewinds and climbs again.
intent: A real product surface with every state finished — queued, uploading, failed, retrying, done, empty, disabled — built on one mechanic (the preview resolving with the upload) on a flat light ground, which is the interface work Herb asked for over abstract demos.

**The five things and what I did about them:**

1. **Row exit was silently dead.** `udz-enter`'s `animation-fill-mode: both` pinned `opacity: 1` and `translateY(0)` forever, and a filling animation beats a transition in the cascade — so `[data-exiting] { opacity: 0 }` never applied and removing a file just squashed the row at full strength, while adding one popped the container open with no height motion. Rebuilt enter and exit as paired animations (`udz-row-open`/`udz-row-close` on the height, `udz-rise`/`udz-fall` on the body), so rows now grow in and fold out on both ends.

2. **The first frame was empty.** Five files sitting at 0%, every thumbnail fully blurred, every ring blank, footer reading `0 of 5 done · 0.0 of 172.3 MB` — the mechanic the piece is about was invisible at load.
